# tests/test_deduplicate_sorted.py
import pytest

# Adapt the import below to match the real location of the function
from your_module import deduplicate_sorted


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "given, expected",
    [
        # Happy-path examples
        ([1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4], [1, 2, 3, 4]),
        (["a", "a", "b", "b", "c"], ["a", "b", "c"]),
        # Edge cases
        ([], []),                     # empty list
        ([42], [42]),                 # single element
        ([5, 5, 5, 5], [5]),          # all items identical
        ([1, 2, 3, 4], [1, 2, 3, 4]), # already unique
    ],
)
def test_deduplicate_general(given, expected):
    """
    Covers the happy path and several edge-case inputs.
    """
    assert deduplicate_sorted(given) == expected


def test_unsorted_input_keeps_nonconsecutive_duplicates():
    """
    The implementation only removes **consecutive** duplicates, so an
    unsorted list still contains repeated values. This documents (and
    therefore guards) that behaviour.
    """
    data = [1, 2, 1, 2]
    # Because the duplicates are not adjacent, the function cannot
    # eliminate them.
    assert deduplicate_sorted(data) == [1, 2, 1, 2]


def test_none_as_input_treated_like_empty():
    """
    `None` is falsy; the first branch (`if not lst`) is taken, so an empty
    list is returned.  The function doesn’t raise but silently converts.
    """
    assert deduplicate_sorted(None) == []


def test_non_sequence_input_raises_type_error():
    """
    A truthy, non-subscriptable input (e.g. an int) passes the initial
    truthiness check and fails at `lst[0]`, raising `TypeError`.
    """
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        deduplicate_sorted(123)

Explanation of test coverage
• Happy path – typical list with duplicates of homogeneous types.  
• Edge cases – empty input, single element, all duplicates, already unique list.  
• Behaviour with unsorted input – confirms duplicates are only removed when consecutive.  
• Error cases –  
  – `None` (falsy) is accepted and returns `[]`, documenting the implicit design decision.  
  – An integer (truthy but not indexable) triggers `TypeError`, showing how the function fails with an invalid type.
